results.title: Programmatic Management for the ABEX CubeSat in a Model Based System Engineering Environment
results.abstract: View Video Presentation: https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2021-0623.vidThis paper describes how the systems engineering team has applied a Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) methodology to the Alabama Burst Energetics eXplorer (ABEX) project, formerly known as the Alabama Experiment for In-situ Shielding (AEGIS). The MBSE approach is based around the development of an Integrated Systems Model (ISM) that contains a model of the system and most of the programmatic information about the project. This paper details how the programmatic aspects of the projects were adapted to be recorded and tracked in the ISM.

results.title: Using a Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) Variant Approach for Architecting Signal Processing in a Space-Based Sensor
results.abstract: Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) can be used to develop the architecture of a space-based sensor. The process begins with the development of use cases (UCs) of a general system model for a sensor processor which is composed of both hardware and software-based elements. Domain-specific UC?s can then be created and linked to the general level. This process continues through the modeling of variances in system behavior, including activity, sequence and state diagrams. This is done in parallel with the development of structural model instances that represent the configuration of the system for the specific domain being considered. The result is an end-to-end extensible sensor model that can then be applied to analyze the end-to-end signal processing chain.
